passage:
I sit behind Rekha in Civics, so I saw it all. Mr Sen was checking notebooks, and hers was missing the last assignment. "Careless, lazy, and probably proud of it," he said, loud enough for the whole room. A few people laughed. Rekha's ears went red. She stared at her desk and didn't answer. I can't say what she was thinking; she just held her pen very still. At break she went and stood alone in the corridor. Next morning she told me she had written down what he said, the date and who was sitting near her. Her father was coming to meet the coordinator. She asked if I'd tell them what I heard. I said yes. I don't know if that helps, but she nodded, and her shoulders looked a little less tight.

Charu, Class 9

qa.q: What did Mr Sen say about Rekha's missing assignment?
qa.a: He said "Careless, lazy, and probably proud of it" loud enough for the whole room.

qa.q: What did Rekha's behaviour after the remark suggest she was feeling, according to Charu?
qa.a: Charu can't be sure, but the red ears, the stillness and the walk to the corridor alone suggest shame. Her silence could also mean she was too shaken to answer.

qa.q: What could Charu do to support Rekha?
qa.a: Tell the coordinator what she heard if asked, stay friendly with Rekha, and not gossip about it. 🙂

qa.q: How might Rekha have felt when Charu said yes to being a witness?
qa.a: Probably relieved not to be alone with it. She nodded and her shoulders looked a little less tight, which suggests the support mattered.

grounding: An observer describes a classmate publicly shamed by a teacher and her response of keeping a record and telling a parent.

passage:
In the Class 10 physics lab, Hansa ma'am picked up Gurleen's lab record and read one wrong reading aloud, slowly, to the whole class. "Twenty-five years of teaching, and I have never seen such foolishness. Maybe you should go back to Class 5." Some students laughed. Gurleen stood there with her face on fire, wishing the floor would open.
At lunch she hid in the washroom. Then she took out her rough notebook and wrote down every word ma'am had said, with the date and time.
That evening she told her father. He read the notebook twice. "Beta, this says something about her conduct, not about you." He wrote to the school coordinator that night.
The next afternoon, the coordinator, Mr D'Costa, met Gurleen and her father. He said, "Thank you for keeping such a clear record. What happened was not acceptable. I will speak to Hansa ma'am today, and I'll check in with you next week."

qa.q: What did Hansa ma'am read aloud from Gurleen's lab record?
How did Gurleen feel when Hansa ma'am mocked her?
qa.a: She burned with shame and humiliation, wishing the floor would open.

qa.q: Which steps did Gurleen take, and why were they wise?
qa.a: She wrote down the words with the date and time, told her father that evening and went to the coordinator, so the adults could act on facts.

qa.q: How does Mr D'Costa see what happened?
qa.a: He sees the teacher's words as unacceptable, thanks Gurleen for her record and promises to act the same day.

grounding: A teen humiliated by a teacher in front of the class keeps a written record and tells a parent and coordinator.

passage:
Dear Reena Bua,
You asked why I sounded so quiet on the phone on Sunday. I'll tell you now.
Last Wednesday in social science, Mr Bhalla made me stand up and said, "Look at him. Head full of cricket, nothing else. Some people are born average." Everyone stared. I felt my face burn. I wanted to run out.
I didn't cry in class. At home I wrote down exactly what he said, the date and the time, like you taught me to do when something feels wrong.
I showed Papa that night. He said it was about Mr Bhalla's behaviour, not about me. On Thursday Papa and I met the coordinator. She read my notes and said, "This should never have happened. I'll speak to him today and check on you next week."
I still feel ashamed sometimes, Bua. But I'm starting to believe it wasn't about me.
Your nephew,
Divyansh

qa.q: What did Mr Bhalla say about Divyansh's head?
qa.a: That it was full of cricket, nothing else.

qa.q: How did Divyansh feel when Mr Bhalla singled him out?
qa.a: He felt deep shame and humiliation, face burning, wanting to run out.

qa.q: Which steps did Divyansh take, and why are they wise?
qa.a: He kept a written record, told Papa that night and went to the coordinator, so the problem was reported with facts.

qa.q: How does the coordinator respond to Divyansh's notes?
qa.a: She takes it seriously, says it should never have happened, promises to speak to Mr Bhalla that day and to check in with Divyansh.

grounding: A teen humiliated by a teacher before the class keeps a written record and tells a parent and the coordinator.
